risk_if_not_implemented: Without Defining Business Context & Mission, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives (R-GV-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Risk Management Program
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls that are aligned with:
(1) The organization's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM); and
(2) Industry-recognized cybersecurity risk management practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Risk Management Program (RSK-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Defining Business Context & Mission (GOV-06) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to proactively govern Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by:
(1) Defining technical security, compliance and resilience requirements; and
(2) Performing a criticality analysis at predefined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
compensating_control_2.justification: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition (PRM-09) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Defining Business Context & Mission (GOV-06) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
